newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper weakness puts pressure on aluminium.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper weakness puts pressure on aluminium.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
More weakness is expected in copper after it hit six-month lows on Friday and broke below a long-term uptrend line, dealers and analysts said.
Aluminium was pressured lower early on Monday as it came under the influence of copper and would be volatile ahead of August contract pricing in later ring trading, they added.
COPPER -
Prices were seen sliding further after the market went into contango on Friday and sustained big losses. The market was also eyeing renewed selling in world stock markets.

"Clearly after such a major break on the weekly chart, there is likely to be further fresh selling at the beginning of this week, but fresh shorts may wait for a two-day or even a two-week close below the trend before going aggressively negative," said broker GNI in a commentary.
Prices crumbled below $2,200 in late inter-office trading on Friday and slid lower early on Monday to support around $2,170.
The $2,170 support level was based on early February 1997 lows of $2,166 and $2,177.

There was scope for more movement on the downside, with next support seen in a band from $2,150 to $2,140, the low of late January 1997, analysts said. The 14-day RSI at Friday's close was around 35, above the oversold level of 30.
"First target on the downside is around $2,150, but a move to $1,850 is quite conceivable in the medium term," GNI added.
At 0745 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,168/73, down $27 from Friday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
The market was hit by the weakness in copper, falling below several support levels early on Monday, traders said.
"It's come under the influence of copper. There has been Far East selling this morning and long liquidation. I think we're looking at $1,650/55," one trader in Europe said.
"But the market is fundamentally strong so I think we'll see a bounce," another said.
The market fell to around $1,660 in early on Monday, finding some support at the 30-day moving average of $1,659.
But the 10-day moving average was helping to put pressure on the market, since it had recently topped out and was turning lower, broker Brandeis noted in a commentary.
Trading would be jumpy with "Third Wednesday" pricing coming in later ring trading, but several analysts believed any weakness was a good buying opportunity.
"Overall, aluminium remains robust and still looks a buy on any further weakness, looking to recover above $1,615/20," said broker Gerald in a commentary.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,662/65, down $32 from Friday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
